review_method: One subagent read the exact configuration sources and classified each case; the primary reviewer then independently checked all 25 against the generator, browser runtime, controls, grader, verifier, and solver where present.

classifications.decisive_evidence: Road and water lanes evolve by world tick; collision, support, and water carry depend on when each hop occurs.
Persistent throttle, brake, steering, and tracking controls must be changed as the hovercar, barriers, and dwell target evolve.
The generated flood, lock, capsule, and circuit state changes only as a synchronous result of labelled actions; the current visible state is sufficient.
Held movement continues through 20 ms navigation ticks and must be sustained, stopped, and redirected; LIDAR returns also age and disappear.
The D1 simplified workflow is a synchronous visible close, select, transfer, remap, and arm sequence; no past or timing information affects success.
A visible guide determines the one placement. The subsequent toppling is an automatic transition that can be ignored before certifying its static result.
Persistent tilt is integrated into velocity and position on every physics tick, so the agent must observe motion and repeatedly redirect or level the board.
All four D3 ring targets move sinusoidally and the strings must track them for 56 consecutive samples across two acts.
Two pods and three apertures move continuously while persistent fan levers spool and alter each pod's trajectory.
D2 still has a moving pod, three moving apertures, and persistent LIFT, COAST, and PRESS fan states requiring motion-based correction.
The five D2 systems include continuous pressure, charged chord releases, an inertial dial, and moving packet interception.

Physics advances only on discrete actions, and the current tick, speed, and all three delayed feed states are visible together. A cautious stateless controller can brake until the feeds stabilize, then position one axis at a time.
D4 hides die faces under housings. Choosing routes for the coupled top sum requires retaining earlier face reveals and the intervening roll order.
D1 explicitly permits the same socket and seal state for all five covenants, so the shuffled reconstruction can repeat one state without remembering any scene mapping.

Full interaction must acquire each object at its screen position on an autonomously moving carousel. This is the moving-screen-target case in the definition; the real-time audit also labels this configuration real-time.
A fixed broad orbit satisfies the exploration ledger, after which one nonzero endpoint view separates every detached branch tip from its stem. Comparing or remembering views is unnecessary.
Persistent eight-way tilt drives autonomous momentum and collisions, requiring repeated observation and correction through the ordered lamps.

After fixed exhaustive quota scans, the agent can leave a hot X slice at quarter-turn one. That current slice exposes all three target coordinates, and locking neither clears nor redraws it, so earlier slice content need not be remembered.
After the view is frozen, held movement, gravity, and jumping evolve every physics tick and must be coordinated with the projected ledges.
The target moves and has a transient event; D5 requires a stable 1.02-second ten-sample shutter hold while framing and focus remain valid.
Full mode requires continuously tracking the moving pressure plate with a held pointer while independently steering for at least 4.5 seconds.
A fixed button sweep satisfies the orbit quota, and one final off-axis screenshot reveals all detached depth gaps before static fruit and basket clicks.
The prompt and drawing state are static. Simplified clicks advance a synthetic plot clock and interpolation supplies timing samples, so a valid first drawing needs no timing or past state.
Each new debugger step anonymizes the previous row. Reconstructing each directed edge requires retaining the prior source and branch when its later destination appears.
As in case 22, a fixed orbit can satisfy the ledger and one final D2 endpoint view, with even larger depth gaps, suffices for static plucking.
